entry.summary:
<p>Identification, security and privacy are represented as a separate dimension in GEA-NZ as they enable and constrain all other layers of the architecture. They can be viewed as interrelated foundational business capabilities that agencies need to have in place to operate safely.</p>
<p>Privacy and security are essential to trust in government, and robust identification of staff, customers and suppliers is a critical enabler of privacy and security. It is important to understand, nevertheless, that ‘identification’ does not necessarily imply explicit naming of parties to an interaction: modern privacy-by-design focuses on ensuring that interactions are authorised and comply with policy, without requiring the unnecessary disclosure of information. So, for example, a person should be able to identify themselves to a trusted party and prove their eligibility for a service, and then present that proof to a service provider without disclosing their identity directly.</p>
<p>An agency enterprise architecture might choose to broaden this dimension to cover all capabilities relating to the management of risk. In any case, a mature and business-driven approach to risk is essential for the effective management of identification, privacy and security: all risk-management involves prioritisation, trade-offs and risk acceptance which require domain expertise and judgment; simple checklist or rules-based approaches will not suffice and may impose unsustainable cost for no effective benefit.</p>
<div class="table-wrapper" tabindex="0" aria-labelledby="table-4" role="region">
<table class="table table-std"><caption id="table-4">
<h3><b>Table 4:&nbsp;</b>How identity, privacy and security influence other dimensions</h3>
</caption>
<thead>
<tr>
<th scope="col">Dimension</th>
<th scope="col">Influence</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Strategy, investment and policy</td>
<td>Identification, privacy and security are strategic capabilities that need targeted investment. They are fundamental to trust in government and a prerequisite for digital transformation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Governance and performance</td>
<td>
<p>Privacy and security are primary focus areas in corporate governance. Every agency is required to nominate accountable executive roles.</p>
<p>Performance monitoring is required, and robust identification of customers, staff and suppliers is a critical enabler.</p>
<p>Privacy and security also impose constraints on some aspects of monitoring.</p>
</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Standards</td>
<td>Standards created or selected to support an agency's business must meet identification, privacy and security requirements.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Business&nbsp;</td>
<td>Identification, privacy and security are business functions in their own right, but are also considerations that enable and constrain customer interaction, channel design, sourcing, service design and process design.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Data, information and analytics</td>
<td>Identification, privacy and security provides access, security and privacy input and constraints for collection, storage and exchange of information.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Application and software services</td>
<td>Identification, privacy and security drive requirements in the selection and operation of technology services.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Infrastructure</td>
<td>Identification, privacy and security are capabilities that require infrastructure investment, and also represent requirements that other infrastructure elements must not compromise.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
